## Context / Problem
Scheduled Mirror Guard run 32567576681 (2026-08-22T10:25:45Z) failed its replication check — Gerrit main SHA != GitHub main SHA — during a heavy merge burst; the next scheduled run (32568260546, +16 min) passed. The mirror was trailing by minutes: expected, self-healing replication lag, not an outage. A red run on main for this primes agents/operators to investigate a non-issue (same noise class as the 3ff9-a8f0 operator ruling: "suppress under normal load — noise, not outage signal").

RCA (see the Phase 1 comment on this ticket, confirmed at runtime): `replication_verdict` (src/rebar/mirror_guard.py:44-73) reports instantaneous SHA equality by design — its own docstring (lines 47-50, shipped in introducing commit d96628c9dca) states transient divergence (~15s post-submit) is expected and "the *alarm's* evaluation window (sustained divergence) absorbs transient lag". The secondary watcher implements that window (infra/terraform/monitoring_ws7.tf:40-44: 2x5-min sustained, "so the normal ~15s post-submit replication lag never pages"). The primary watcher (.github/workflows/mirror-guard.yml) never got one: it runs `python -m rebar.mirror_guard --replication` once and fails on a single instantaneous sample. Classification: incomplete-implementation — the designed lag-absorption was never built on the workflow surface. caused_by: a774-5ca9-3a80-4f6d (scope-of-work; the omission shipped with a774's own commit d96628c9dca).

## Approach
Give the guard an in-process, scheduler-agnostic evaluation window in `src/rebar/mirror_guard.py` (this satisfies project.portability: the tolerance lives in the module, not in any CI provider's retry/state machinery — comparing against the previous run via the Actions API was rejected as GitHub-specific with no portable fallback). This approach fits because it implements exactly the absorption the module's own docstring already delegates to the alarm layer, using the same "sustained divergence" semantics the sibling CloudWatch alarm already encodes:

- Keep `replication_verdict(gerrit_sha, github_sha)` unchanged (it correctly reports the instantaneous truth; its contractual schema test at tests/unit/test_mirror_guard.py:104 is superset-pinned `set(v) >= {...}`).
- Add a persistence wrapper `replication_check_with_lag_tolerance(fetch_pair, *, attempts=3, delay_seconds=45.0, sleep=time.sleep) -> dict`: fetch (gerrit_sha, github_sha); if the sample is in sync OR a SHA is missing, return that verdict immediately (one fetch, zero sleeps — the common healthy case pays nothing; missing-SHA keeps today's immediate-failure behavior). On divergence, sleep `delay_seconds` and re-sample, up to `attempts` total samples; return healthy the moment a sample converges (annotated `"samples": n`, reason "transient replication lag, converged"). If all samples diverge, return the last unhealthy verdict with `"samples"` and a reason distinguishing a static GitHub tip ("replication stalled") from a moving-but-not-converged tip. Any non-converged outcome still fails — strictly no weakening: today's failure set minus lag-that-converges-within-the-window. A GitHub-ahead/foreign divergence (true invariant breach) never converges to the Gerrit SHA, so it still fails every run.
- `run()` (src/rebar/mirror_guard.py:184, existing symbol confirmed by reading the tree) gains keyword params `lag_attempts: int = 3`, `lag_delay_seconds: float = 45.0`, `sleep=time.sleep` and drives the replication check through the wrapper; fetch exceptions keep propagating to the existing except -> exit 2 path. Defaults: 3 samples x 45s spacing (~90s window, ~6x the documented ~15s expected lag) unless flags say otherwise.
- `main()` gains `--lag-attempts` / `--lag-delay` flags wired to those params (defaults as above).
- `.github/workflows/mirror-guard.yml`: header comment updated to state the new semantics (fails when divergence persists across the in-run window; transient post-submit lag self-clears) — no functional workflow change.
- Module docstring updated: the CLI itself now provides the alarm-layer evaluation window portably; the CloudWatch alarm remains the secondary sustained-divergence pager.
- Keep every touched function under the McCabe ceiling (wrapper is a small loop; run() gains no branches beyond the call swap).

## Scope
- src/rebar/mirror_guard.py — persistence wrapper, run()/main() params + flags, docstring.
- tests/unit/test_mirror_guard.py — new behavioral tests for the tolerance window; update `test_run_divergence_exit_1` (line 141) to inject a no-op sleep so it exercises the persistent-divergence path without real sleeping (assertion `code == 1` unchanged).
- .github/workflows/mirror-guard.yml — header comment only.

## Testing
All unit-level, monkeypatched fetchers, injected no-op sleep — no network, no real sleeping (the suite's socket guard already forbids network):
- Happy path: first sample in sync -> healthy, exactly 1 fetch and 0 sleep calls (counted via the injected fakes).
- Bug reproduction (RED first): fetch sequence diverged -> converged; today this exits 1 (single sample), after the fix it is healthy / exit 0 with reason noting convergence.
- Failure path kept loud: all samples diverged with static GitHub tip -> unhealthy, exit 1, reason names stalled replication and sample count.
- Failure path kept loud (ahead/foreign): all samples diverged with a moving, never-converging GitHub tip -> unhealthy, exit 1.
- Edge: missing SHA on first sample -> immediate unhealthy verdict, no re-sampling.
- Contractual: existing schema/exit-code tests still pass unchanged (schema is superset-pinned).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A fetch sequence [diverged, in-sync] through `run(check_replication=True, ...)` with injected no-op sleep returns exit code 0 and a healthy replication verdict (new unit test, seen RED on unfixed code first).
- [ ] A fetch sequence of 3 diverged samples with a static GitHub SHA returns exit code 1 with a reason containing "stalled" and `samples == 3` (new unit test).
- [ ] A fetch sequence of 3 diverged samples with a moving, never-converging GitHub SHA returns exit code 1 (new unit test — GitHub-ahead stays loud).
- [ ] An in-sync first sample performs exactly one fetch-pair call and zero sleep calls (new unit test).
- [ ] A missing-SHA first sample returns unhealthy immediately without re-sampling (new unit test).
- [ ] Full tests/unit/test_mirror_guard.py passes; `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` (new=0, increased=0) all pass in the worktree venv.
- [ ] .github/workflows/mirror-guard.yml header describes the persistence semantics (comment-only change, verified by reading the diff).
